title: fix(fields,core,detail): make the sharing-rule dialog usable — i18n, a picker that lists people, and permission-aware CTAs
body:
Fixes the Console's "New sharing rule" dialog, which could not produce a working rule. Server-side half is objectstack-ai/objectstack#3821 / objectstack-ai/objectstack PR (framework branch `claude/sharing-rules-i18n-recipient-02a623`).

## What was broken

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| Recipient picker showed **"No matches"** for every type | `$orderby: 'name asc'` fell into the `Object.entries` branch of `queryParamsToRecord` and was walked character by character into `0 n,1 a,2 m,…`; the server sorted by columns that don't exist and returned nothing |
| Dialog copy was English in a Chinese Console | The three sharing-rule widgets hardcoded their strings and never used `useFieldTranslation` |
| Reopening a saved rule **blanked the recipient** | The picker's type-change reset treated the edit form's `'' → 'user'` hydration as a type switch, and the blank was then persisted on save |
| "Add filter" fired validation / could save early | No `FilterBuilder` control set `type="button"`; a bare `<button>` in a `<form>` defaults to submit |
| A rejected save showed `FORBIDDEN: insufficient privileges to update showcase_private_note pi-TgoJ4_DM55Fqz` | The form rendered `error.message` verbatim — untranslated, and leaking the object machine name and record id |
| **"Edit" offered on read-only records** | Object permissions can't express "this one record is read-only", which is exactly what a read-only sharing grant is |

`ObjectGrid` builds the same string `$orderby` from a schema-level `sort` in three places, so this also fixes grids that silently rendered an empty table.

## Notable design points

- **The recipient placeholder is keyed per type**, not interpolated. `` `Select a ${type.replace(/_/g,' ')}` `` is a shape no locale can translate.
- **The record-level gate consults the explain engine** (`POST /api/v1/security/explain` with a `recordId`, ADR-0090 D6 / ADR-0095 C2) — the same pipeline the enforcement middleware runs, so button and server can't disagree. Explaining oneself needs no special permission.
- **It fails open everywhere**: no answer yet, non-OK response, a deployment without `plugin-security` (501), a split SPA origin. A courtesy hint must never be why a permitted user can't act; the server stays the authority (ADR-0057 D10).
- ⚠️ **Reviewer call:** the gate costs one cached `explain` request per record open (skipped when the object-level check already says no). Happy to move it behind a server-side per-record access hint on the record read instead if you'd rather not pay that.

## Verification

Browser-driven against the framework showcase Console in Chinese — data, accounts, rules and checks all created through the UI, no API calls:

- Copy localized throughout; picker lists real users / business units / positions (empty "teams" is genuinely 0 rows)
- A rule saved end-to-end stores a real record id; reopening it keeps recipient + criteria
- Editing the filter no longer submits the dialog
- Read-only recipient: **no Edit button**; same recipient at `edit` level: **Edit present, save succeeds**; the user's own records keep Edit throughout
- Denied save now reads 「您没有权限保存这条记录。」 — no machine name, no record id

Tests: `plugin-detail` + `permissions` 303 ✓, `components` 319 ✓, `fields`/`core`/`i18n` suites ✓. Each new test verified to fail without its fix. Two known-unrelated flakes on this machine: a TZ-dependent `DATEFORMAT` case that also fails on `main`, and `ReportPreview.dataset` timing out only under full-suite load (passes in isolation on both branches).
